title: PM–Eng 1:1 scratchbook — API / Console / Dedicated / Private
content:
Context / purpose:
- Quick scratchbook for my weekly 1:1 with Evan (eng lead) — focus: unblock roadmap for Q2 features across API, Console, Dedicated, Private.
- Use this doc as noisy brain-dump: agenda, concrete asks, numbers to verify, and follow-ups to push into Jira/Linear after the meeting.

Top things I want to cover (high priority):
1) API streaming stability incidents last month
   - Symptom: ~3x spike in partial-response errors for streaming endpoints between 2026-02-14 and 2026-02-18.
   - My ask: quick postmortem summary + action items (owner + ETA). Who owns the streaming retry logic? Suspect edge proxy vs runtime kernel interaction.
   - Data I want Evan to confirm during 1:1: error percent by model variant, affected regions, and whether Dedicated customers saw same.

2) Console rollout for rollout policies UI (canary + fallback)
   - Status: design sign-off done; engineering PR in flight (PR #482).
   - Blocker: backend route for policy audit logs not fully spec'd — need SRE input on retention + perf.
   - Ask: commit to finish backend hooks by end of sprint or push minimal MVP that stores audit events in s3/long-term store.

3) Dedicated capacity autoscaling behavior
   - Recent customer report: burst scaling latency ~4–6 minutes causing throttling on heavy inference bursts.
   - Hypothesis: current scale-up policy uses average CPU vs request queue depth. Might need a reactive policy based on queue length/KV cache pressure.
   - Ask Evan: can we prototype queue-depth-based autoscaler in sandbox cluster? Rough estimate of effort?

4) Private deployment (VPC) timeline and packaging
   - Sales asked for on-prem install option for a prospect with air-gapped requirement — want rough delivery ETA for internal roadmap.
   - Concern: packaging + KMS/HSM integration might be the critical path.
   - Ask: confirm minimal deliverables for 1st private bundle (control plane only vs full on-prem) and list dependencies.

Quick data nuggets to verify in-meeting:
- Current API 95th latency (text generation) — last weekly dashboard showed 220 ms; is that still accurate?
- Token cost delta with new batching: estimate 12–18% token cost reduction on median workloads (need Evan to sanity-check).
- SLO burn rate for ded-dev customers last 30 days.

Agenda (10–15m cadence):
- 0–3m: quick personal check-in (one new book rec?)
- 3–8m: Align on top 3 product/infra blockers (pick 1–2 to deep dive)
- 8–12m: Decisions needed now (console audit logs approach, autoscale experiment)
- 12–15m: Assign owners, set explicit next steps + due dates

Possible deep-dive: streaming errors root cause hypotheses
- Edge proxy timeouts vs long polling behavior when KV cache warmed (older sessions).
- Tokenizer mismatches in streaming path causing partial flushes.
- Backpressure propagation missing from runtime -> proxy -> client path.
- Ask to Evan: which team should I loop in for a hotfix? Runtime infra or gateway?

Draft follow-ups I want from Evan (assign during 1:1):
- Evan: short postmortem outline for streaming incidents (by 2026-03-17). Include: timeline, component owners, quick mitigation, long-term fix.
- Infra (Evan/infra): triage autoscale behavior and propose two config options (queue-depth trigger, faster warm pools) — draft config by 2026-03-24.
- Eng (runtime): confirm if model-variant fallbacks are enabled in Dedicated when a node fails — test plan + result by 2026-03-20.
- Me (Alex): convert action items to Linear and link to roadmap JIRA.

Notes to self / talking points:
- Emphasize minimal viable audit log: route+user+timestamp+change, store cold; avoid perf hit on control plane.
- For autoscale, lean towards conservative warms rather than aggressive immediate scale — customers prefer transient throttling over noisy scale flips. But need data to back.
- Private: propose 2-phase delivery: (1) control-plane-only container bundle + KMS shim; (2) full on-prem runtime images.

Open questions I want Evan to answer:
- Who is the owner for streaming retry heuristics? (runtime team lead?)
- Do we have capacity to take on the autoscale sandbox prototype in the next sprint or do we prioritize bug fixes?
- Is there appetite to expose a customer-facing flag for Dedicated that toggles aggressive scale (for extra cost)?

Random scratch / drafts to copy into Linear tickets after 1:1:
- TITLE: streaming-partial-response-postmortem
  DESC: brief timeline, impact metrics (requests, failed streaming sessions), suggested mitigations (proxy timeouts, backpressure fix, better retries).

- TITLE: console-audit-logs-backend
  DESC: MVP: store events to s3; schema: route, user, action, ts, model_version, rollout_id. Retention configurable by org. Non-blocking: surface a small in-console viewer that queries s3 via pre-signed URLs.

- TITLE: dedicated-autoscale-queue-trigger
  DESC: implement queue-length trigger + warm-pool reserve. Experiment in sandbox, measure scale-up latency.

Meeting aftermath checklist (what I'll do right after 1:1):
- 1) Capture Evan's verbal commitments and owners -> create Linear issues (labels: 1on1, unblock, infra)
- 2) Email SRE + runtime leads with context and ask for short sync (include relevant RED/JIRA links)
- 3) Update product roadmap board with revised ETA if decisions change

Tone notes for convo:
- Keep it tactical and bounded (avoid turning into full planning). Goal: leave with at least 2 concrete next actions and dates.
- Validate tradeoffs out loud (cost vs latency vs dev effort) — Evan appreciates numbers not just opinions.

Misc small reminders:
- Bring up customer quote from ACME pilot on Dedicated throttling (copy in thread)
- Check whether we can reuse existing KMS connector code from internal infra for Private deployment (ask Maya to surface repo link if needed).

End-of-doc — quick TODO queue (shorthand):
- [ ] PM: make Linear tickets after 1:1 (today)
- [ ] Evan: streaming PM postmortem (03/17)
- [ ] Evan/Infra: autoscale config drafts (03/24)
- [ ] Runtime: dedicated fallback test results (03/20)

-- notes-to-self: keep this messy; move clean items out to proper docs.
